daily.title: What does Trump's midterm elections loss mean for strained US-India ties?
daily.summary: Donald Trump's electoral setback might give New Delhi and Washington space to reset relations, but there is no guarantee that the US will actually change its approach to India.

daily.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
daily.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

daily.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
daily.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

daily.title: North Korea tells EU to 'mind its own business' on human rights
daily.summary: North Korea's UN mission has lashed out at the European Union over a draft UN resolution. Pyongyang has said the West does not have a monopoly on human rights.

daily.title: Poland arrests four over alleged spying for Russia
daily.summary: Poland has charged four people with espionage, saying they were sending information to Moscow. Two more have been accused of shipping military components to Russia.

daily.title: Finland court jails captain and crew member over Baltic cable sabotage
daily.summary: Finland seized the Fitburg freighter last year over the suspected sabotage of cables linking Helsinki and Tallinn. It's one of several incidents of damaged infrastructure in the Baltic since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

daily.title: Several European flights receive bomb threats, some divert
daily.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

daily.title: South Korea tests Arctic shipping route amid Russia-West row
daily.summary: For South Korean ships, navigating off the north coast of Russia dramatically reduces travel time to Europe, but the pro-Ukraine coalition might see it as undermining their efforts to isolate Moscow.

daily.title: Germany news: Deportations on the decline
daily.summary: Despite a decrease in overall deportations, more people were sent back to Turkey. Volkswagen is facing a fresh 'Dieselgate' trial. And Germany's leading DAX stock index hit a new high. DW has more.

daily.title: France braces for fresh protests as unions strike over higher wages
daily.summary: Unions representing the education sector, rail employees, public hospitals and postal services called the strike. Authorities have deployed some 70,000 police and security officers across the country.

daily.title: India news: ​​Several feared trapped as building collapses in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar
daily.summary: Rescue operations are ongoing as a building collapsed in Chawri Bazaar. Meanwhile, "Ramayana," starring Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi, has hit theaters. Follow DW for more.

daily.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
daily.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

daily.title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 more years
daily.summary: Joshua Wong, once a teen activist and one of the faces of the "Umbrella Movement," is spending most of his adult life so far in prison.

daily.title: NASA's Swift space telescope plunges back to Earth in fiery demise
daily.summary: NASA's Swift orbital observatory fell back to Earth after running its mission for more than two decades. A rescue attempt to raise its sinking orbit had earlier failed.

daily.title: Democrats take House and Senate from Republicans in US midterm rout
daily.summary: Democrats will control both chambers of Congress after flipping seats in Republican strongholds across the US in an election seen as a repudiation of President Donald Trump.

daily.title: Bavarian politician Hubert Aiwanger found dead in Berlin hotel
daily.summary: Aiwanger was Bavaria's Economy Minister and the chairman of the right-wing populist Free Voters party. The circumstances surrounding his death are still unclear.

daily.title: Winners, losers, the EU: Five takeaways from the US midterms
daily.summary: Donald Trump's Republicans suffered a crushing defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, with the Democrats wresting control of Congress. What does this mean for US politics and the world?

daily.title: 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
daily.summary: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

daily.title: Fact check: Examining viral narratives after the US midterm elections
daily.summary: As Democrats celebrate major gains, false claims about election fraud have spread. Viral posts alleging illegal voting and election rigging are intended to fuel doubt about the integrity of the vote. DW checks the facts.

daily.title: French blood banks targeted by refrigerator cyberattack
daily.summary: A cyberattack had attempted to destroy blood plasma by raising the temperatures in cold storage facilities past the boiling point.

daily.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
daily.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

daily.title: Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
daily.summary: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

daily.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
daily.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

daily.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
daily.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

weekly.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
weekly.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

weekly.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
weekly.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

weekly.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
weekly.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

weekly.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
weekly.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

weekly.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
weekly.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

weekly.title: Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
weekly.summary: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

weekly.title: Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
weekly.summary: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

weekly.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
weekly.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

weekly.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
weekly.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

weekly.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
weekly.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

weekly.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
weekly.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

weekly.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
weekly.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

weekly.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
weekly.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

weekly.title: Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
weekly.summary: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

weekly.title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
weekly.summary: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

weekly.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
weekly.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.

weekly.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
weekly.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

weekly.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
weekly.summary: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

weekly.title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
weekly.summary: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

weekly.title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
weekly.summary: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.

weekly.title: Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
weekly.summary: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

weekly.title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
weekly.summary: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.

weekly.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
weekly.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

weekly.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

weekly.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
weekly.summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

weekly.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
weekly.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

weekly.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
weekly.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

weekly.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
weekly.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

weekly.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
weekly.summary: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.

weekly.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
weekly.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

weekly.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
weekly.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

weekly.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
weekly.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

weekly.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
weekly.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

developing.title: Live: Fresh protests hit France amid heightened security
developing.summary: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as thousands participate in a new round of protests. The protest location was changed last minute in Paris. Follow DW.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
